info.title: Prosp Discovery API
info.summary: B2B prospect discovery — run a discovery job, poll it, read the prospects.
info.description:
Customer-facing REST API for the Prosp prospect-discovery platform. Run a discovery,
poll it to completion, then read and acknowledge the companies it found. The API
returns only customer-safe fields — internal scoring, provenance, and raw content are
never included in any response.

## Canonical flow (REST)
1. `POST /api/v1/discoveries` — start a discovery, by saved ICP id or inline criteria
   (costs credits; an `X-Idempotency-Key` header makes the call safe to retry).
2. `GET /api/v1/discoveries/{jobId}` — poll this until `status` is terminal
   (`completed`/`failed`/`exhausted`); the `result` block appears once the run finishes.
3. `GET /api/v1/discoveries/{jobId}/prospects` — read the companies this run found
   (or `GET /api/v1/prospects` for the de-duplicated inbox across all your discoveries).
4. `POST /api/v1/prospects/ack` — acknowledge delivery so a company isn't returned again.

The `/mcp/*` job endpoints (`/mcp/tools/execute`, `/mcp/jobs/{jobId}/status`, …) are a
fully supported alternative surface with equivalent semantics; the `/api/v1/*` resources
above are the recommended REST entry point for new integrations.

## Auth
OAuth2 **client-credentials** (OpenID Connect). Exchange your `client_id` +
`client_secret` for a Bearer token at the token endpoint (see the security scheme
below for the exact URL), then send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every call.
Tokens carry the `mcp/execute` scope.

## Errors
Every error shares one shape — `{ error, message, request_id }`. Quote `request_id`
in support tickets. Errors are always signalled by the HTTP status code; there are no
`200`-with-error responses.

## Changelog
- **0.4.0** — The finished-discovery contract now matches what the gateway actually serves.
  ADDED to `JobResult`: `terminal_reason`, `already_owned_count`, `candidates_screened` and
  `evaluated_count` — all four were already being served on `GET /mcp/jobs/{jobId}/result` and
  on the `result` of `GET /api/v1/discoveries/{jobId}`, and are the same values (from the same
  reader) that `JobStatus` reports while the run is live. ADDED to `ProspectDetail`: the
  envelope-root `domain`, served on every detail response. REMOVED from `JobResult`:
  `total_cost_usd`, `total_rejections`, `auto_completed`, `fallback_occurred`, `duration_ms`
  and `sources_used` — these are internal run-level fields the customer boundary has always
  stripped, so no client can have received them; documenting them promised data the API does
  not return. Not a breaking change in either direction: nothing that was served stopped being
  served.
- **0.3.0** — Converged the per-discovery delivery count onto ONE canonical name across
  surfaces: `JobStatus` now carries `total_prospects` (the same name and metric as
  `JobResult.total_prospects`, read as a live snapshot). The former `JobStatus.prospectsFound`
  is retained as a DEPRECATED alias (identical value) for a back-compat transition and will be
  removed in a future major version. The pagination `total` on `ProspectList`/`ProspectSummaryList`
  is a separate, explicitly-documented concept (a list/search result-set count) — not the
  per-discovery delivery count. No breaking change: `prospectsFound` still ships.
- **0.2.0** — Added the `/api/v1/discoveries*` (merged status + result) and `/api/v1/icps`
  resources, plus the discovery summary on `JobResult` (`completed_at`,
  `total_prospects`; the `sources_used` / `duration_ms` / `total_cost_usd` members of that
  summary were never served and were removed from the contract in 0.4.0).
- **0.1.0** — Initial release.

get.description: Reports whether the API and its backing services are healthy. No auth required. Read-only - only GET and HEAD are accepted; any other method returns 405 with an `Allow` header.

405.description: Method not allowed (only GET and HEAD are accepted).

503.description: Service temporarily unavailable (a backing dependency is unreachable).

post.description:
Debits 100 credits (the per-discovery cost) atomically and queues a discovery. The
`X-Idempotency-Key` header is **required**; replaying the same key returns the
original job with `deduplicated: true` and does not double-charge.

**Concurrency limit.** A tenant may run only a bounded number of discovery jobs at once.
While you are at that limit a new `execute` is rejected with **429** and
`error: concurrent_limit` — cancel or wait for a running job to finish, then retry. The
credits for a rejected request are **refunded**, so a 429 never costs you credits (your
balance nets to zero and no ledger entry is written for the rejected attempt).

**Saturation pre-check (net-new estimate).** Before charging, the service estimates how
many *new* companies this exact ICP would yield for you (companies you do not already own
from prior runs). When that estimate is ~0 and reliable — you have already discovered the
addressable set for these criteria — the request is held with **409** and a
`status: saturation_warning` body (see `SaturationWarning`) instead of running. **No credits
are charged and no job is started.** To run it anyway, re-submit with
`parameters.acknowledge_low_yield: true`; the acknowledged run charges normally and starts.

200.description: Job queued, OR the existing job when the request was de-duplicated — by a replayed idempotency key, or by a query-fingerprint match against a discovery you already started. A de-duplicated response carries `deduplicated: true` + `reason` and is NOT charged (the credit debit is refunded). Distinguish the two shapes via `deduplicated`.

402.description: Insufficient credits (balance below the per-discovery cost).

409.description: Pre-flight warning, run held — a **saturation warning** (this ICP would yield ~0 net-new companies for you), an **ICP-mismatch warning** (the targeting is a material mismatch for your product/offering; a corrected ICP is offered under `suggestions`), or a **low-yield prediction warning** (ICPs like yours historically under-delivered). **No credits were charged and no job was started.** Re-submit with `parameters.acknowledge_low_yield: true` to run and be charged anyway.

get.summary: Get the caller's current credit balance.
get.description:
Returns the authenticated customer's credit balance and the per-job cost. Check this
before `execute` (which debits `job_cost` and returns 402 when the balance is short).

Returns the authenticated customer's credit transactions — debits (discovery-job charges),
refunds, and manual adjustments — newest first, reconstructed from durable job and refund
markers. EVERY row carries a signed `amount` in credits, so a client can `sum(amount)` to
reconcile the ledger against `balance`. `limit` bounds the number of TRANSACTIONS returned
(a single job can contribute up to two rows — a debit and its refund) and `offset` selects a
stable page; `total` + `has_more` let a client walk the full reconstructable history. The
ledger is a BOUNDED WINDOW: markers older than `window_start` (≈7 days) have expired and can
no longer be reconstructed — `history_incomplete=true` signals such older history exists
(`truncated` is a separate this-page hard-cap signal, always false here).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of transactions to return (newest first). Rejected with 400 if 0/negative or above 500.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of transactions to skip from the newest, for paging. Rejected with 400 if negative.

get.description: Returns each of the caller's jobs as a lean `{jobId, status}` summary. Poll `GET /mcp/jobs/{jobId}/status` for a single job's progress detail.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque progressive-polling cursor. Pass the previous response's `next_cursor` to receive only the prospect domains added since that poll. Omit for the full `found[]` accumulated so far.

get.summary: Fetch a completed job's result summary.
get.description:
Returns the result once the job reaches any terminal state:
`completed`, `failed`, `exhausted`, or `cancelled`. A `cancelled` job
returns the prospects it had already delivered before cancellation (it is
terminal-with-data, not a perpetual 202). Non-terminal states return the
current status with a "not yet complete" message.

202.description: The job has not reached a terminal state yet. Poll again; this body carries the current status and never partial results.

post.description:
Stops a running discovery, releasing its concurrency slot so a new `execute` can start.
Credits are refunded on the server side (see `credits_refunded`) only when the run had
delivered **zero** prospects at cancel time; if prospects were already delivered you keep
them and are not refunded. Those already-delivered prospects remain retrievable after
cancellation via `GET /mcp/jobs/{jobId}/result` and `GET /api/v1/discoveries/{jobId}`
(`cancelled` is a terminal state that carries its delivered results).
Only the job's owner may cancel it. Cancelling an already-terminal job is a no-op that
returns the job's current state.

200.description: The job's post-cancel state (and any refund applied).

get.description: An alias of `GET /api/v1/prospects` with identical semantics. New integrations should use `GET /api/v1/prospects`.

get.summary: List the caller's prospects across all discoveries (de-duplicated).
get.description:
The customer-wide prospect inbox. **With no `job_id` (default):** returns one row
per company across every discovery the caller has run — if the same company was
re-discovered by multiple jobs, the newest re-discovery wins (de-duplicated).
**With `job_id`:** narrows to that single job and returns its per-discovery rows
(one per company↔job edge), i.e. the same result as
`GET /api/v1/discoveries/{jobId}/prospects`.

Undelivered prospects only, unless `include_delivered=true`. Responses contain only
customer-safe fields; internal scoring and provenance fields are never included.

For a single run's results, prefer `GET /api/v1/discoveries/{jobId}/prospects`.
For semantic ranking, see `GET /api/v1/prospects/search`.

get.summary: Semantic search over the caller's prospects (lean summaries + progressive cursor).
get.description:
Returns LEAN prospect summaries (~11 customer-safe fields) — not the full record — so the
response can never exceed the client token budget. To read every field for one company,
call `GET /api/v1/prospects/{domain}` with a summary's `domain`.

Pagination is a progressive OPAQUE cursor: omit `cursor` for the first page, then pass the
previous response's `next_cursor` back verbatim to fetch the next. Treat it as opaque — do
not parse or construct it (its encoding is an implementation detail); an unrecognized cursor
safely restarts from the first page. `has_more=false` / `next_cursor=null` means you have
seen everything above the relevance floor — stop.

200.description: A lean, capped page of ranked summaries (each carries a `semantic_score`).

post.description:
Marks one or more domains delivered so they aren't returned again. **Job-blind by design:**
one ack marks each domain delivered across all of the caller's jobs. **Idempotent:** an
unknown or already-acknowledged domain is a harmless no-op (returns `200` with a count that
reflects only the records actually marked), so clients never need to special-case them.

get.summary: Prospect detail by domain (customer-safe fields + enrichments).

200.description: Prospect detail. `status` is `active` or `delivered` (a known company).

get.description:
Newest-first page of the caller's discoveries. Page with `limit` (default 50, max 200)
and `offset`. A `limit` outside 1–200, a negative or non-integer `limit`/`offset`, or any
other query parameter, is rejected with `400 invalid_query`.

200.description: The caller's discoveries, with the canonical pagination envelope (`total`, `count`, `offset`, `has_more`) shared with the credit-ledger surface so a client pages every list surface the same way.

customer_id.description: The authenticated customer these discoveries belong to.

count.description: Number of discoveries in THIS page (never exceeds the requested `limit`).

total.description: Total discoveries for the caller (across all pages).

offset.description: The starting index this page was served from (echoes the request `offset`).

has_more.description: True when this page left discoveries unreturned — fetch the next with `offset += count`.

post.summary: Trigger a discovery (by ICP id or inline criteria).
post.description:
Debits 100 credits (the per-discovery cost) and queues a discovery. The body is EITHER
`{icpId}` (runs a saved ICP's criteria) OR inline `DiscoveryCriteria` — mutually exclusive,
and ENFORCED: mixing them is a `400 schema_validation_failed` rejected before any debit,
never a silent "the saved ICP won and your inline fields were discarded". The lone
exception is the warn-and-confirm control `acknowledge_low_yield`, which may accompany
`icpId`. `X-Idempotency-Key` is required. An unknown `icpId` refunds the debit and
returns 404.

200.description: Queued, or the existing job for a duplicate (idempotency key or query).

409.description: Pre-flight warning, run held — a **saturation warning** (this ICP would yield ~0 net-new companies for you), an **ICP-mismatch warning** (the targeting is a material mismatch for your product/offering; a corrected ICP is offered under `suggestions`), or a **low-yield prediction warning** (ICPs like yours historically under-delivered). **No credits were charged and no job was started.** Re-submit with `acknowledge_low_yield: true` to run and be charged anyway.

get.summary: Merged discovery view (status + result when terminal).

200.description:
Always returns the current status; includes `result` once terminal
(`completed`, `failed`, `exhausted`, or `cancelled`). A `cancelled` run's
`result` carries the prospects it delivered before cancellation.

get.summary: List the prospects one discovery run found (per-run view).
get.description:
The discovery-scoped sub-resource: "what did **this** run find." Always a single
job, returning its per-discovery rows (one per company↔job edge) — not
de-duplicated against the caller's other jobs. Undelivered prospects only, unless
`include_delivered=true`. Tenant-scoped by the token; the `jobId` never crosses
tenants.

This is the per-run equivalent of `GET /api/v1/prospects?job_id={jobId}`. For the
de-duplicated view across all of the caller's discoveries, use
`GET /api/v1/prospects` with no `job_id`.

post.summary: Create a saved ICP (Ideal Customer Profile).

parameters.name: icpId
parameters.description: The id of the saved ICP.

get.summary: List the caller's grounded circular-economy opportunities.
get.description:
The set of circular-economy opportunities inferred from YOUR OWN stored business profile:
for each, the flow, asset, capacity or capability it rests on and the kind of company that
completes it. Costs no credits and runs no search.

The list is served from an already-computed portfolio and is dated by `computed_at`, which
is when it was DERIVED - not when you asked. It is never padded: one grounded opportunity
yields one entry.

**Read `speech_act` before you use a label.** An element whose `grounding` is `IMPLIED` is
a hypothesis - it carries `speech_act: ASK` and may only ever be put as a question, never
stated as fact. The two elements are graded independently and mean different things: the
`resource` is a claim about YOUR OWN business, the `counterpart` is a hypothesis about
which kind of company would want it.

`outreach_draft_eligible` answers only whether the entry may GROUND a draft, and it turns
on the `resource`, because that is what a message would be about. An entry may be
draft-eligible while its `counterpart` is still `ASK` - that is the ordinary case, not an
edge case - and in that case the market hypothesis still may not be asserted in the
message. Running one requires you to confirm or correct the resource first; see
`POST /api/v1/discoveries` with `opportunityHandle`.

Order is server-authoritative and is not a ranking you should re-apply - the same order is
used on every surface these opportunities appear on.

/api/v1/tenant/odoo-connection.description:
Self-serve onboarding for your Odoo CRM connection. You submit your own Odoo destination
and credentials; the connection is live-tested (and any stage/team/user id validated)
before anything is saved, and stored encrypted-at-rest. Your identity comes from the
access token — a body `customer_id` that disagrees with it is rejected. The `odoo_api_key`
is write-only: it is never returned on any response. `odoo_url` must be a public http(s)
host — a URL resolving to a private, loopback, link-local, reserved, or multicast address
is rejected with `422 unsafe_url`.

post.summary: Submit / activate this tenant's Odoo connection.

200.description: Connection re-validated and updated (a connection already existed).

400.description: Malformed body or a `customer_id` that disagrees with the token identity.

403.description: The token identity is reserved-unrouted and can never map to an Odoo.

409.description: The destination is already registered, or an onboarding is in progress.

422.description:
Unprocessable — the live connection test failed, an FK id does not exist,
`odoo_url` resolves to a non-public (internal) address (`error: unsafe_url`), or
host validation timed out (`error: url_validation_timeout`, fail-closed).

503.description:
Tenant-registry unavailable — either not configured on this deployment
(`error: registry_unavailable`) or the backend is temporarily unreachable
(`error: registry_degraded`, `retryable: true`, with a `Retry-After` header —
safe to retry with backoff).

get.summary: Get this tenant's registered Odoo connection (no secrets).

404.description: No Odoo connection registered for this tenant.

503.description:
Tenant-registry unavailable — either not configured on this deployment
(`error: registry_unavailable`) or the backend is temporarily unreachable
(`error: registry_degraded`, `retryable: true`, with a `Retry-After` header —
safe to retry with backoff).

200.description:
Revoked (idempotent). `status` is `revoked` when a connection existed and was
removed, or `not_connected` when nothing was registered (no-op).

503.description:
Tenant-registry unavailable — either not configured on this deployment
(`error: registry_unavailable`) or the backend is temporarily unreachable
(`error: registry_degraded`, `retryable: true`, with a `Retry-After` header —
safe to retry with backoff).

cognitoClientCredentials.description:
OAuth2 machine-to-machine using the `client_credentials` grant (OpenID Connect; the
OpenAPI `flows.clientCredentials` object below). This is the ONLY supported grant — do
NOT use the interactive `authorization_code` flow that the identity provider's discovery
document may advertise; it is for a different (user-facing) client and rejects M2M.
Your `client_id`/`client_secret` are issued per customer (via the Telegram
`/credentials` flow). POST them to the `tokenUrl` below to obtain an access token, then
send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request.

scopes.mcp/execute: Start and manage discoveries and read prospects.

IdempotencyKey.name: X-Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Client-generated key that makes `execute` safe to retry.

JobId.name: jobId
JobId.description: The discovery's id, as returned when you started it.

JobIdQuery.name: job_id
JobIdQuery.description:
Narrow to a single discovery. Also switches the listing from the de-duplicated
customer-wide view to that job's per-discovery rows. Never crosses tenants.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum number of prospects to return per page (1–200; defaults to 50). A value outside the range is rejected with a 400, not clamped.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: Number of prospects to skip before the page starts, for offset pagination (defaults to 0).

SearchLimit.name: limit
SearchLimit.description: Page size for search (1–50, default 20). Deliberately smaller than the list `limit`; a value outside the range is rejected with a 400, not clamped.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque progressive-pagination cursor. Omit for the first page; pass the previous response's `next_cursor` back verbatim to fetch the next. Treat it as an opaque token: do NOT parse it, construct it, or do arithmetic on it — its internal encoding is an implementation detail that may change without notice. An unrecognized or malformed cursor is safely treated as "start from the beginning" rather than rejected.

Country.name: country
Country.description:
Narrow to one or more ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, case-insensitive
(`country=sk` or `country=SK,CZ` — comma-separated, no repeated `country=` keys).
Matches the delivered company's `country_code`. Checked against the real ISO 3166-1
alpha-2 list; an unrecognized code is rejected with `400 invalid_query` naming the
value, before any other processing. A HARD filter on this read only — it does not
change what a discovery targets or delivers, and `total` always counts the filtered
set (never the caller's whole, unfiltered inbox).

NotOwner.description: The token's tenant does not own this job.

MethodNotAllowed.description: HTTP method not allowed on this endpoint (rejected before any credit debit).

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded (100 requests / 60s per customer).

TooManyRequests.description: Request throttled. `error` is `rate_limit_exceeded` when the 100-requests/60s per-customer window is exceeded, or `concurrent_limit` when the tenant already has the maximum number of discovery jobs running. On `concurrent_limit` the request's credits are refunded (no charge).

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the window resets (rate-limit case only).

JobNotComplete.description: The in-flight answer to a result poll: the job exists and is still running, so there is nothing terminal to return yet. Deliberately OPEN to additional properties — the fields below are what the surface sends today, and a poll response is not the place to fail a customer's client over an added key.

message.description: Human-readable detail, e.g. "Job not yet complete".

ok.description: `false` while the job is still running — results are not available yet, keep polling. This is NOT an error: no `error` code accompanies it.

http_status.description: Echo of the HTTP status (202), so a client reading only the body can branch on it.

request_id.description: Correlation id — quote this in support tickets about a stuck poll.

Error.description: The single error shape for the whole surface.

error.description: Stable machine-readable code. Common values include: `invalid_token`, `insufficient_credits`, `method_not_allowed`, `rate_limit_exceeded`, `concurrent_limit`, `missing_idempotency_key` (the required `X-Idempotency-Key` header was absent on `execute`), `schema_validation_failed` (request body failed the OpenAPI schema — rejected before any credit debit), `validation_failed` / `icp_not_found` (the discovery criteria were malformed / matched no ideal-customer profile — no job created, any debit refunded), `invalid_query` (an unknown or malformed search/list query param), `invalid_job_id`, and `not_owner`.

request_id.description: Correlation id — quote this in support tickets.

toolName.description: The tool to run. Use `discovery` to start a prospect discovery.

IcpRequest.description: Body to create or replace a saved ICP — an optional display name plus the discovery criteria.

name.description: Optional human-readable label for this ICP.

criteria.description: The saved discovery criteria this ICP re-runs.

Icp.description: A saved Ideal-Customer-Profile — reusable discovery criteria you can re-run by id.

icpId.description: Server-assigned unique id for this ICP; pass it to `POST /api/v1/discoveries` to run it.

name.description: The display name you gave this ICP.

criteria.description: The discovery criteria stored in this ICP.

updatedAt.description: When the ICP was last updated (ISO-8601).

TenantOdooConnectionRequest.description:
Your own Odoo destination and credentials for self-serve onboarding. `odoo_api_key`
is write-only (accepted here, never returned). `odoo_url` must be a public http(s)
host — private, loopback, link-local, and reserved addresses are rejected.

odoo_url.description: Public https base URL of the tenant's Odoo instance.

odoo_db.description: Your Odoo database name — one of the four API authentication parameters (alongside `odoo_url`, `odoo_uid`, `odoo_api_key`). An Odoo server can host multiple databases, so this identifies which one to sync leads into. Leads are written through Odoo's JSON-RPC API — no direct database access is used. If unsure, find it at `https://<your-odoo-host>/web/database/list`.

odoo_uid.description: The Odoo user id the API key belongs to.

odoo_api_key.description: Odoo API key used to authenticate. Write-only — accepted here but never returned on any response.

stage_id.description: Optional Odoo CRM stage id to place new leads in. Validated to exist before the connection is saved.

team_id.description: Optional Odoo sales-team id to assign new leads to. Validated to exist before the connection is saved.

user_id.description: Optional Odoo user id to assign as the salesperson on new leads. Validated to exist before the connection is saved.

enrichment_stage_id.description: Optional Odoo CRM stage id for leads awaiting further contact enrichment. Validated to exist before the connection is saved.

lead_type.description: Whether new records are created as CRM leads or opportunities. Defaults to `opportunity` when omitted.

TenantOdooConnection.description:
Your registered Odoo connection, without any secrets. `validated_at` and `message`
are present only on a successful submit response. The `odoo_api_key` and any other
credential material are never included in this response.

customer_id.description: Your tenant identifier (derived from the access token).

odoo_url.description: The Odoo base URL leads are written to.

odoo_db.description: Your Odoo database name — the API authentication parameter identifying which database on the Odoo server leads are synced into. Leads are written through Odoo's JSON-RPC API; no direct database access is used.

odoo_uid.description: The Odoo user id the stored API key belongs to.

stage_id.description: The configured Odoo CRM stage id for new leads, or null if unset.

team_id.description: The configured Odoo sales-team id for new leads, or null if unset.

user_id.description: The configured Odoo salesperson user id for new leads, or null if unset.

enrichment_stage_id.description: The configured Odoo CRM stage id for leads awaiting enrichment, or null if unset.

lead_type.description: Whether records are created as leads or opportunities.

validated_at.description: When the connection was last successfully validated (present only on a submit response).

message.description: Human-readable outcome of the submit (present only on a submit response).

TenantOdooConnectionRevoked.description: Result of revoking your Odoo connection.

status.description: `revoked` when a connection existed and was removed; `not_connected` when nothing was registered (idempotent no-op).

TenantConnectionError.description:
Error shape for the CRM-connection onboarding endpoints. Distinct from the API-wide
`Error`: it omits `request_id`, and the body never exposes a resolved IP address or
other internal detail.

ValidationError.description: A 400 response carrying one or more field-level criteria violations.

message.description: Human-readable summary of what failed validation.

field.description: Name of the request field that failed validation.

DiscoveryCriteria.description:
The criteria that describe the companies you want to find. Only `query` is required;
the other fields narrow and steer the search. `maxResults` must be 1–200 (a value outside
the range is rejected with a 400), and invalid `company_sizes` values are likewise rejected
with a 400 rather than silently ignored. Unknown fields are rejected with a 400 that names
the offending property.

query.description: Free-text description of the companies you want to discover. The primary search signal.

industries.description: Target industries. Prospects are scored for fit against these; companies in unrelated industries are filtered out.

locations.description: Target countries or regions to search within (e.g. country names). Restricts results to companies located there.

company_sizes.description:
Company-size buckets to include, by employee headcount. Any combination of:
`micro` (≤10), `small` (up to ~50), `medium` (up to ~200), `large` (up to ~500),
`enterprise` (500+). Omit to allow any size. Each bucket maps to a
`company_size` value; request `micro` to prioritize the ≤10-employee shops, which are
returned with `company_size: micro` (the output `company_size` uses the SAME lowercase
tokens as this input filter, so a value read off a result can be re-submitted verbatim).
NOTE: this filter is ADVISORY, not strict — in thin markets the engine may relax it
to adjacent buckets and still deliver e.g. `micro` under a `small` request (this is
disclosed at delivery via a `FILTER_RELAXED` suggestion). So omitting a size does not
guarantee its exclusion; it expresses preference, not a hard exclusion.

keywords.description: Additional keywords or phrases to bias the search toward (e.g. products, technologies, or capabilities).

exclusions.description: Domains or terms to exclude from results — e.g. competitors, existing customers, or your own brand. Matching companies are dropped from discovery.

sub_country_regions.description:
ISO-3166-2 sub-country regions (e.g. states or provinces) to focus the search within a
country. Validated against the supported region set. This is a REGIONAL PREFERENCE, not a
hard filter: companies located in the requested region(s) are prioritized (ranked higher
for relevance), which can substantially raise the in-region share of your results, while
companies OUTSIDE those regions are still returned, ranked lower. It is a precision dial —
expect fewer but more-targeted results, trading total volume for regional focus. Omit it
(or clear it) to broaden coverage across the whole country. When this field is set, the
discovery result's `suggestions` array discloses the relaxation: a `FILTER_RELAXED` region
suggestion (naming the filter, with a `{sub_country_regions: []}` correction) when returned
companies with a known region fall outside the request, otherwise an informational
`REGION_PREFERENCE_APPLIED` note — both carrying the same one-tap correction.

target_business_models.description:
Optional value-chain-role filter. When set, only companies whose classified
business model is one of these roles are kept; a prospect whose role is a confirmed
member of none is dropped. Use e.g. `["manufacturer"]` for manufacturers only, or
`["distributor"]` for wholesale distributors only. Omit to accept any role
(default — no role filtering).

website.description: Your own website. Automatically excluded from results so you never discover yourself.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of prospects to return for this discovery (1–200; a value outside this range is rejected with 400, not clamped; defaults to 50).

language.description:
Optional market-language hint as an ISO-639-1 code (e.g. `de`, `cs`, `pl`). Steers the
query→ICP expansion so keyword/industry expansion is generated in the market's language
rather than inferred solely from `query`. Advisory, not a hard filter — company and person
names are never translated, and results are not restricted to a single content language.
Omit to let the engine infer the language from `query` itself.

SaturationWarning.description:
Returned with **409** by `POST /mcp/tools/execute` (and `POST /api/v1/discoveries`) when the
saturation pre-check estimates this ICP would yield ~0 net-new companies for you and the
estimate is reliable. **No credits were charged and no job was started.** Re-submit the same
request with `parameters.acknowledge_low_yield: true` to run and be charged anyway.

expected_new_companies.description: Estimated number of net-new companies (not already owned by you) this run would yield.

acknowledge_param.description: The request parameter to set to `true` on re-submit to run anyway (`acknowledge_low_yield`).

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the warning and how to proceed.

request_id.description: Correlation id — quote it in support tickets.

IcpMismatchWarning.description:
Returned with **409** by `POST /mcp/tools/execute` (and `POST /api/v1/discoveries`) when the
ICP-coherence pre-check judges the draft targeting (industries/keywords/query) to be a
material mismatch for the seller's own product/offering — e.g. a warehouse-fulfillment-robotics
seller targeting small grocery/food retail. **No credits were charged and no job was started.**
A corrected-ICP suggestion is offered under `suggestions[]`. Re-submit the same request with
`parameters.acknowledge_low_yield: true` to run the original ICP anyway and be charged. Only
produced when the seller has a stored profile/offering; skipped otherwise (the run proceeds).

acknowledge_param.description: The request parameter to set to `true` on re-submit to run anyway (`acknowledge_low_yield`).

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the mismatch, the corrected ICP, and how to proceed.

suggestions.description: A single corrected-ICP suggestion (better-fit industries/keywords/query for the offering).

request_id.description: Correlation id — quote it in support tickets.

LowYieldPredictionWarning.description:
Returned with **409** by `POST /mcp/tools/execute` (and `POST /api/v1/discoveries`) when the
learned ICP-outcome corpus predicts this draft ICP will materially under-deliver (ICPs like
yours historically returned few results). **No credits were charged and no job was started.**
Re-submit the same request with `parameters.acknowledge_low_yield: true` to run and be
charged anyway. Rides the same warn-and-confirm channel as `SaturationWarning` /
`IcpMismatchWarning` — one acknowledgement parameter clears all pre-flight warnings.

acknowledge_param.description: The request parameter to set to `true` on re-submit to run anyway (`acknowledge_low_yield`).

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the prediction and how to proceed.

suggestion.description: A bounded, leak-safe advisory (e.g. broaden the ICP) — no counts or cross-customer data.

request_id.description: Correlation id — quote it in support tickets.

JobAccepted.description: Returned when a discovery has been accepted and queued for processing.

jobId.description: Id of the newly queued discovery. Use it to poll status and read results.

status.description: Always `queued` — the discovery has been accepted and will start shortly.

poll_after_seconds.description: Recommended number of seconds to wait before polling this discovery's status again. A cadence hint for polite back-off — poll no more often than this rather than hammering the API.

estimated_duration_seconds.description: Expected wall-clock duration for this discovery, in seconds — the single planning-safe number, always present. Equals the p95 of recent OBSERVED job runtimes (the industry-standard user-facing UPPER BOUND so a slow-but-healthy run is not mistaken for a stuck one, and a client planning timeouts is not misled low): it is identical to `estimated_duration_p95_seconds` once history exists, and falls back to a static coarse default until enough jobs have finished. For the full percentile trio read `estimated_duration_p50_seconds` / `estimated_duration_p90_seconds` / `estimated_duration_p95_seconds`. An estimate, not a guarantee.

estimated_duration_p50_seconds.description: Median (p50) of recent OBSERVED job runtimes, in seconds — the TYPICAL duration. The lowest member of the explicit p50/p90/p95 trio; `estimated_duration_p95_seconds` is the planning-safe upper bound. Omitted (together with the p90 and p95 fields) until enough jobs have finished to derive it.

estimated_duration_p90_seconds.description: 90th-percentile (p90) of recent OBSERVED job runtimes, in seconds — a monitoring-baseline percentile and the middle member of the explicit p50/p90/p95 trio. Omitted (together with the p50 and p95 fields) until enough jobs have finished to derive it.

estimated_duration_p95_seconds.description: 95th-percentile (p95) of recent OBSERVED job runtimes, in seconds — the planning-safe user-facing UPPER BOUND, and the top member of the explicit p50/p90/p95 trio. This is the same value carried by `estimated_duration_seconds` whenever history exists (that field is the always-present single number; this one is the labelled member of the trio). Omitted (together with the p50 and p90 fields) until enough jobs have finished to derive it.

estimated_yield.description: Expectation-setting hint: the TOTAL number of prospects this discovery is likely to DELIVER — i.e. total deliverable, NOT net-new. It is projected from YOUR own historical delivery ratio (prospects delivered ÷ target requested, accumulated across your completed discoveries) applied to this run's requested target, and it is never projected above the request. "Total deliverable" means the count is GROSS: it includes domains you may already own from a prior discovery (see `already_owned_count` on the status/result for how many of the delivered set were already yours); it is not a promise of that many BRAND-NEW companies. The projection is deliberately CONSERVATIVE (it tracks your historical delivery ratio and empirically under-predicts a fast-converging run), so on the status poll it is floored at the live `prospectsFound` — the value shown is `max(frozen_estimate, prospectsFound)` and therefore never sits BELOW the count already delivered in the same response. Omitted entirely (never null) until you have enough completed-discovery history to project honestly. An estimate, not a guarantee.

DuplicateResponse.description: Returned instead of a new job when the request matched a discovery you already started.

jobId.description: Id of the existing discovery the request was matched to.

deduplicated.description: Always `true` — this response indicates the request was de-duplicated onto an existing job.

reason.description: Why the request was de-duplicated: `idempotency_key` = you replayed the same idempotency key; `duplicate_query` = an identical discovery is already running.

AcknowledgeLowYield.description:
Set to `true` to run this discovery even when the saturation pre-check estimates ~0
net-new companies (see the `409 saturation_warning` response on `POST /mcp/tools/execute`).
The acknowledged run charges normally and starts. Omit (or `false`) for the default
behaviour, where a saturated ICP is held with a `409` and NOT charged. Not a search
criterion — it steers the warn-and-confirm gate only, which is why it is the ONE field
that may accompany `icpId` in a `DiscoveryTrigger` body.

DiscoveryTrigger.description:
The body for starting a discovery. Provide EITHER a saved ICP id OR inline criteria —
mutually exclusive, and enforced: a body carrying `icpId` alongside any search criterion
(`query`, `industries`, `locations`, `keywords`, `company_sizes`, `exclusions`,
`maxResults`, `language`, `website`) is rejected with `400 schema_validation_failed`
BEFORE any credit is debited, rather than silently running the saved ICP's criteria and
discarding the inline ones. The single exception is `acknowledge_low_yield`, which is a
warn-and-confirm control rather than a search criterion: `{icpId, acknowledge_low_yield}`
is how a saved ICP held by a `409` is re-submitted to run anyway.

icpId.description: Id of a saved ICP to run. Its stored criteria are used for this discovery.

opportunityHandle.description: The `handle` of one entry from `GET /api/v1/opportunities`. Opaque, and resolved against YOUR OWN portfolio - it names a graded opportunity, never a search. An unknown handle refunds the debit and returns 404.

confirmedResource.description: Your own description of the resource, REQUIRED when the entry's `requires_resource_confirmation` is true (its resource is an unconfirmed hypothesis). Without it the run is refused with 404 `resource_confirmation_required` and the debit is refunded - an inferred hypothesis may not be used to target a search until you have confirmed or corrected it. What you send is RETAINED as a stated fact about your business and informs later inference, so correct it rather than echoing ours back.

Discovery.description: A discovery's status merged with its result. The `result` block is present only once the discovery reaches a terminal state.

status.description: Current lifecycle state of the discovery.

result.description: The finished discovery result. Present only when `status` is terminal.

JobIcpId.description: The saved ICP this discovery was started from (`POST /api/v1/discoveries {"icpId": ...}`), for billing attribution — the same value the matching credit-ledger rows carry, so a charge reconciles back to the ICP that caused it. Served on EVERY job surface (the progressive status, the merged discovery view, the finished result, and each entry of the discoveries list) from one reader, so a customer can attribute a run to its ICP without waiting for the run to finish or cross-referencing the ledger. ABSENT (field omitted, never an empty string) when the run was ad-hoc from inline criteria. Ids are scoped to the calling customer — the same namespace `GET /api/v1/icps` returns.

TerminalReason.description: Why the discovery stopped, once terminal; null while still running, and null on any job terminal before this field's writers shipped. Carried on BOTH the progressive status and the finalized result — they read the same durable value, so the two surfaces cannot disagree about why a run ended. `candidates_exhausted` = the market had no more matching candidates to evaluate, and every candidate it did dispatch was evaluated; `trailing_candidates_forgiven` = the run stopped while a small remainder of its own candidates (up to 5%) was still being evaluated, so the shortfall was forgiven rather than exhausted — reported separately from `candidates_exhausted` because the two call for OPPOSITE responses: a genuinely dry market wants a wider profile, whereas a forgiven remainder means the run was cut short and re-running the SAME profile may deliver; `candidate_cap_reached` = when a run's candidates ran out before your target, it fetched further batches of new candidates, and it stopped because it had screened the maximum number of candidates one run may evaluate — the sources were still returning new candidates, so the shortfall reflects the per-run screening limit, not an exhausted market; `candidate_search_failed` = the run's candidates ran out before your target and the search for further candidates failed repeatedly, so the market was never shown to be exhausted — re-running the SAME profile later may deliver; `time_limit_reached` = the run hit its time budget while still producing; `stalled_no_progress` = the run stopped producing results and was terminated early rather than hitting its budget (a different situation from either of the two above, and reported separately so it is not mistaken for a thin market or a short budget); `fan_in_incomplete` = a search step never finished, so the run was never able to ask for more candidates; `target_reached` = the run delivered everything you asked for; `saturated_known_set` = every delivered domain was already yours from an earlier search (refunded); `cancelled_by_customer` = you cancelled it via `POST /mcp/jobs/{jobId}/cancel`. When credits are refunded, the refund reason matches this.

AlreadyOwnedCount.description: How many of this discovery's delivered domains you ALREADY owned from a PRIOR discovery (any earlier search, not just this one's filters) — i.e. cross-search overlap with your existing prospects. 0 means every delivered domain is new to you. Domains already owned under this exact search's filters are de-duplicated out before delivery and are not counted here. Served on both the progressive status and the finalized result from one durable value. See `already_owned_withheld_count` for how many WERE de-duplicated out.

AlreadyOwnedWithheldCount.description: How many companies this discovery found, judged in-scope for THIS search, and then did NOT deliver because you already own them from an earlier run of the same search. This is the count `already_owned_count` explicitly excludes: those domains were suppressed one step BEFORE delivery, so they appear in neither `prospects` nor `total_prospects`. It is the number that explains an otherwise puzzling result — a repeat search of a market you have already worked returns few new companies precisely BECAUSE most of what it found is already yours, and without this field that outcome is indistinguishable from a failed run. Counted as DISTINCT companies across both suppression paths (freshly searched and re-served from your existing knowledge base), so it never double-counts one company found twice. ABSENT — never 0 — when nothing was suppressed, so any value you receive is a real one.

CandidatesScreened.description: Number of candidate companies this discovery began SCREENING (search/candidate-dispatch phase). Increases monotonically during screening so a client sees live progress even before the first prospect domain lands; 0 before screening has started. It legitimately PLATEAUS once search has exhausted the niche and the run moves into its crawl/validation tail — that is not a stall. For liveness during that tail, read `evaluated_count`. On the finished result it is the frozen final value, so the same number explains a run after it ends.

EvaluatedCount.description: Number of screened candidates that have finished crawl + validation (a running verdict count = accepted + rejected). Complements `candidates_screened`: it keeps climbing through the crawl/validation tail — after screening plateaus — so a polling client sees liveness for the WHOLE run. Retains its final total once the discovery is terminal, where together with `candidates_screened` it is the funnel that explains the delivered count.

JobStatus.description:
Progressive discovery status. While the job runs, `found[]` accumulates the prospect
DOMAINS discovered so far (validated-only — a bare domain is customer-safe), so a polling
client sees results before the job finishes instead of nothing until it ends. Pass the
previous response's `next_cursor` back as the `cursor` query param to receive only the
domains added since the last poll; `has_more` stays true until a terminal state, at which
point `found[]` is served from the finalized result and `next_cursor` is null.

status.description: Current lifecycle state of the discovery.

total_prospects.description: Canonical count of validated prospects this discovery has delivered so far — the SAME per-discovery delivery metric the finalized `JobResult.total_prospects` carries, read here as a LIVE snapshot that grows monotonically while the job runs and equals the terminal `JobResult.total_prospects` once the job is done. Key on this ONE field name to group/count a discovery's delivery across the status and result surfaces. This is a single-job delivery count — NOT the pagination `total` on `ProspectList`/`ProspectSummaryList`, which counts a LIST/SEARCH result set across your whole inbox.

withheld_count.description: How many companies this discovery DELIVERED and then RETRACTED, so `total_prospects` above is the SERVABLE set rather than the originally-announced one. A prospect is retracted when a check that can only complete after delivery decides it does not belong to your search — most often a headquarters re-check placing it outside your target region. Retracted companies are removed from `prospects[]`/`found[]` and never reach your CRM. ABSENT (never `0`) when nothing was retracted: absence is the signal.

withheld.description: The retracted companies, one entry per row removed from `prospects[]`/`found[]`. Present only alongside a non-zero `withheld_count`.

domain.description: The retracted company's domain, as it was originally delivered.

reason.description: Bounded reason the company was retracted. `sub_region` = its headquarters resolved outside your target region; `exclusion` / `business_model` = it matched a filter you set; `kb_seed_dedup` = you already own it from an earlier search; `delivery_cap` = it arrived after the run had already met your target.

prospectsFound.description: DEPRECATED camelCase alias of `total_prospects` (identical value); kept during a back-compat transition so existing clients keying on `prospectsFound` do not break. New integrations MUST read `total_prospects` (the canonical, snake_case name shared with `JobResult`). This alias will be removed in a future major version once no live consumer depends on it.

target.description: Requested prospect target (maxResults); null for jobs predating target persistence.

found.description: Prospect domains discovered so far, in discovery order. With a `cursor`, only the domains added since that cursor; without one, the full list so far. Call `GET /api/v1/prospects/{domain}` (or read the result once terminal) for full detail on any domain.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor to pass as the `cursor` query param on the next poll to fetch only newer domains. Null once the job is terminal (nothing more will accumulate).

has_more.description: True while the job is non-terminal and more domains may still accumulate.

stage.description: Coarse progress phase, a companion to `candidates_screened`. `searching` = still issuing discovery queries, no candidates evaluated yet; `screening` = evaluating candidate companies; `complete` = the job is terminal (finished, whatever its `terminal_reason`).

last_activity_at.description: RFC-3339 UTC timestamp (…Z) of the last per-candidate verdict (accept/reject) — the SAME timestamp format as every other date-time the API surfaces (`discovered_at`, `employee_count_as_of`, `facts[].extracted_at`, credit-ledger timestamps). Present only while the job is RUNNING and at least one candidate has been evaluated; omitted on terminal jobs and before the first verdict. With `seconds_since_last_activity` it distinguishes a working-but-slow job from a stalled one when `candidates_screened`/`evaluated_count` look static during the slow evaluation tail.

seconds_since_last_activity.description: Seconds since `last_activity_at`, computed fresh each poll (resets toward 0 on every new verdict, grows only during genuine silence). Present only while running with at least one verdict — the read-time-fresh liveness signal a polling client uses to tell working-but-slow from stuck.

poll_after_seconds.description: Recommended number of seconds to wait before polling this discovery's status again. A cadence hint for polite back-off — poll no more often than this rather than hammering the API.

estimated_duration_seconds.description: Expected wall-clock duration for this discovery, in seconds — the single planning-safe number, always present. Equals the p95 of recent OBSERVED job runtimes (the industry-standard user-facing UPPER BOUND so a slow-but-healthy run is not mistaken for a stuck one, and a client planning timeouts is not misled low): it is identical to `estimated_duration_p95_seconds` once history exists, and falls back to a static coarse default until enough jobs have finished. For the full percentile trio read `estimated_duration_p50_seconds` / `estimated_duration_p90_seconds` / `estimated_duration_p95_seconds`. An estimate, not a guarantee.

estimated_duration_p50_seconds.description: Median (p50) of recent OBSERVED job runtimes, in seconds — the TYPICAL duration. The lowest member of the explicit p50/p90/p95 trio; `estimated_duration_p95_seconds` is the planning-safe upper bound. Omitted (together with the p90 and p95 fields) until enough jobs have finished to derive it.

estimated_duration_p90_seconds.description: 90th-percentile (p90) of recent OBSERVED job runtimes, in seconds — a monitoring-baseline percentile and the middle member of the explicit p50/p90/p95 trio. Omitted (together with the p50 and p95 fields) until enough jobs have finished to derive it.

estimated_duration_p95_seconds.description: 95th-percentile (p95) of recent OBSERVED job runtimes, in seconds — the planning-safe user-facing UPPER BOUND, and the top member of the explicit p50/p90/p95 trio. This is the same value carried by `estimated_duration_seconds` whenever history exists (that field is the always-present single number; this one is the labelled member of the trio). Omitted (together with the p50 and p90 fields) until enough jobs have finished to derive it.

estimated_yield.description: Expectation-setting hint: the TOTAL number of prospects this discovery is likely to DELIVER — i.e. total deliverable, NOT net-new. It is projected from YOUR own historical delivery ratio (prospects delivered ÷ target requested, accumulated across your completed discoveries) applied to this run's requested target, and it is never projected above the request. "Total deliverable" means the count is GROSS: it includes domains you may already own from a prior discovery (see `already_owned_count` for how many of the delivered set were already yours); it is not a promise of that many BRAND-NEW companies. It derives from the SAME frozen value returned when the discovery was accepted (surfaced here on every poll so a client that did not capture the accept response can still read it), but because the projection is deliberately CONSERVATIVE and a fast-converging run can overtake it, the value shown here is floored at the live `prospectsFound` — i.e. `max(frozen_estimate, prospectsFound)` — so this hint is NEVER less than the count already delivered in the same response. Omitted entirely (never null) when the job carried no create-time projection (insufficient history). An estimate, not a guarantee.

suggestions.description: The SAME data-driven next-step entries `JobResult.suggestions` carries, served here so a client that only ever polls status is not dead-ended on an underperforming run. Read through the one shared reader, so this array can never disagree with the finalized result about which advisories are still true. It has two lives across a discovery's lifetime: while the run is still going it carries AT MOST ONE early `BROADEN_QUERY` entry, emitted only once the observed counters imply the requested target is unreachable, so you can act at minute 5 instead of at the terminal; once the run is terminal it carries that run's frozen advice and disclosures — the underperformance recommendation and any mandatory `FILTER_RELAXED` / `REGION_PREFERENCE_APPLIED` note. ABSENT (never `[]`) when there is nothing to say — absence is the signal, and unlike `JobResult.suggestions` this property has no `[]` default. See `Suggestion` for the per-entry shape and `JobResult.suggestions` for the full terminal vocabulary.

CreditLedger.description: A customer's credit-transaction history (`GET /mcp/credits/ledger`). Every transaction row carries a signed `amount`, so `sum(transactions[].amount)` reconciles the credit movement against `balance`.

customer_id.description: The authenticated customer these transactions belong to.

count.description: Number of transactions in THIS page (never exceeds the requested `limit`).

total.description: Total reconstructable transactions in the window (across all pages). When `history_incomplete` is true this is a lower bound — older, marker-expired history is not counted.

offset.description: The starting index this page was served from (echoes the request `offset`, clamped to `total`).

has_more.description: True when this page left transactions unreturned — fetch the next page with `offset += count`.

window_start.description: RFC-3339 UTC start of the reconstructable window (`now − marker TTL`, ≈7 days). Transactions older than this have expired markers and cannot be reconstructed.

truncated.description: PURE this-page hard-cap signal: true only when an item/byte cap dropped rows from THIS page. The ledger paginates on `offset`/`limit` with no per-page item/byte cap (`has_more` covers the tail), so `truncated` is always `false` here. Retained for a uniform pagination envelope across list surfaces. The "older history exists" signal is the DISTINCT `history_incomplete` field below — do NOT read `truncated` for data completeness.

history_incomplete.description: Data-COMPLETENESS signal (distinct from `truncated`): true when older account history exists that the bounded markers can no longer reconstruct — set in exactly two cases: (1) the customer has more jobs than a single read enumerates (only the newest are scanned), or (2) a job's paired debit/refund fell outside the reconstructable window so one half-pair row was suppressed. When true, the visible rows are still internally consistent but do NOT span the customer's whole account history. A COMPLETE page (`has_more=false`, `count == total`) can still be `history_incomplete=true` — the two flags are orthogonal.

LedgerTransaction.description: One credit-ledger row. EVERY row carries a signed `amount` (credits) — negative for a debit, positive for a refund/grant — so a client can sum the column to reconcile against `balance`. Carries NO internal provenance flags: this is a customer-facing billing surface.

type.description: `debit` = a discovery-job charge; `refund` = credits returned for a terminated/refunded job; `adjustment` = a manual balance change.

job_id.description: The discovery job this row belongs to. Absent on manual adjustments.

icp_id.description: The saved ICP this charge is attributable to — the `icpId` the run was started with via `POST /api/v1/discoveries {"icpId": ...}`. Lets a customer running several saved ICPs reconcile a charge back to the ICP that caused it. Carried on both the `debit` row and its paired `refund` row, so an attribution survives the two landing on different pages. ABSENT (field omitted, never an empty string) for an ad-hoc run started from inline criteria, and on `adjustment` rows, which have no job. Ids are scoped to the calling customer — the same namespace `GET /api/v1/icps` returns.

amount.description: Signed credit movement — negative for a debit, positive for a refund/grant.

balance_after.description: Best-effort: the TRUE balance immediately after this event, present ONLY when a durable post-event snapshot was recorded at the source (`jobs:charged-balance:{jobId}`, written by the gateway debit script). OMITTED (field absent) on rows with no snapshot — historical debits that predate the snapshot feature, and reconstructed/inferred refunds — because a running balance is NOT reliably reconstructable after the fact (concurrent jobs and top-ups make back-derivation unsound). Never fabricated: a null/absent value means "unknown", not zero. Reconcile via the signed `amount` column, which every row carries.

timestamp.description: RFC-3339 UTC timestamp (…Z) of the transaction.

adjustment_id.description: Audit id of a manual adjustment (adjustment rows only).

actor.description: Who performed a manual adjustment (adjustment rows only).

JobSummary.description: Lean job list item (`GET /mcp/jobs`) — identity plus lifecycle state only. For a single job's progress (target, prospectsFound, found[], progressive cursor) call `GET /mcp/jobs/{jobId}/status`.

status.description: Current lifecycle state of the discovery.

JobCancelled.description: Result of `POST /mcp/jobs/{jobId}/cancel` — the job's post-cancel state and any refund applied.

status.description: Lifecycle state after the cancel (`cancelled`, or the existing terminal state if already finished).

credits_refunded.description: Credits returned to the caller's balance for the cancelled run. Null/0 when nothing was refundable.

credits_refund_reason.description: Human-readable reason the refund was (or was not) applied.

JobResult.description:
The result of a finished discovery, present once the run reaches a terminal state.
Field names are snake_case. `prospects[]` carries only customer-safe fields — internal
scoring, provenance, and raw content are never included.

status.description: Terminal lifecycle state of the discovery (`completed`, `failed`, or `exhausted`).

total_prospects.description: Number of prospects this discovery produced — the canonical per-discovery delivery count, the SAME field name and metric the live `JobStatus.total_prospects` reports (this is its terminal, frozen value). Key on this ONE name to group/count a discovery's delivery across the status and result surfaces. On the merged `Discovery` view this is read at `result.total_prospects`. Distinct from the pagination `total` on `ProspectList`/`ProspectSummaryList` (a LIST/SEARCH result-set count across your inbox).

withheld_count.description: How many companies this discovery DELIVERED and then RETRACTED, so `total_prospects` above is the SERVABLE set rather than the originally-announced one. A prospect is retracted when a check that can only complete after delivery decides it does not belong to your search — most often a headquarters re-check placing it outside your target region. Retracted companies are removed from `prospects[]`/`found[]` and never reach your CRM. ABSENT (never `0`) when nothing was retracted: absence is the signal.

withheld.description: The retracted companies, one entry per row removed from `prospects[]`/`found[]`. Present only alongside a non-zero `withheld_count`.

domain.description: The retracted company's domain, as it was originally delivered.

reason.description: Bounded reason the company was retracted. `sub_region` = its headquarters resolved outside your target region; `exclusion` / `business_model` = it matched a filter you set; `kb_seed_dedup` = you already own it from an earlier search; `delivery_cap` = it arrived after the run had already met your target.

auto_complete_reason.description: Present ONLY when automatic recovery force-completed a run that stalled in `processing` with no completion marker (`stuck_processing_no_marker` when prospects had accumulated, `stuck_processing_no_prospects` when none had). Absent on every normally-terminating run.

credits_refunded.description: Credits returned to the caller's balance when this run was auto-refunded (e.g. an exhausted run that delivered fewer prospects than requested). Absent when no refund applied. Same field, semantics, and shape as `JobCancelled.credits_refunded` — one canonical refund projection across the result and cancel surfaces.

credits_refund_reason.description: Bounded reason the refund was applied (e.g. `candidates_exhausted`, `time_limit_reached`), resolved from durable terminal state. Present iff `credits_refunded` is. Mirrors `JobCancelled.credits_refund_reason`.

completed_at.description: When the discovery finished (ISO-8601). Null while not yet terminal.

prospects.description: The customer-safe prospects this run found (same field set as `ProspectList`).

suggestions.description: Data-driven entries derived from THIS run. At most ONE leak-safe ADVICE recommendation (the single most impactful change) is emitted when the run underperformed (exhausted with fewer prospects than requested), each carrying a human-readable message and an optional `suggested_parameters` delta to merge over your original criteria and start a new discovery. In addition, ZERO OR MORE mandatory `FILTER_RELAXED` disclosures may appear on any terminal run when a requested filter (`company_sizes` or `sub_country_regions`) was relaxed so some returned companies fall outside it, each carrying a `suggested_parameters` clearing that filter. For a region-scoped run where no out-of-region company is yet provable (the region signal often finalizes after async enrichment), a single informational `REGION_PREFERENCE_APPLIED` note appears instead, carrying the same `{sub_country_regions: []}` correction. Empty when the run met target, no filter was relaxed, and no regional preference was requested.

circular_opportunity.description: ONE circular-economy opportunity inferred from your own stored business profile, offered alongside this finished run rather than as a separate message. ABSENT - never null and never an empty object - whenever there is nothing well-grounded to offer, you have opted out, or this run was itself started from an opportunity. The same entry is returned for every read of this discovery, so polling does not change it.

CircularClaim.description: One claim, together with what may be DONE with it. `label` is presented verbatim in its original language and is never translated - it may carry a product, brand or material designation. `speech_act` is the machine-readable form of a rule that is a sentence on a chat surface: an `IMPLIED` claim is something we inferred about your business, not something you told us, so it may only ever be put to you as a QUESTION.

label.description: The flow, asset, capacity, capability or counterpart type, in plain commercial language.

grounding.description: `STATED` - appears in your business profile. `CONFIRMED` - you corrected or confirmed it and we retained that. `IMPLIED` - inferred, and not yet confirmed by you.

speech_act.description: `ASSERT` for a stated or confirmed claim. `ASK` for an unconfirmed hypothesis, which must be phrased as a question about your business and must not enter outreach.

CircularOpportunity.description: One graded circular-economy opportunity for your business. Individually runnable via `POST /api/v1/discoveries` with `opportunityHandle`.

handle.description: Opaque id of this entry, scoped to your portfolio. Pass it to run the counterpart search.

category_group.description: The kind of opportunity - materials recovery is one of several and is never a default. A bounded vocabulary; treat an unfamiliar value as opaque rather than as an error.

mode.description: The shape of the search this entry becomes. Bounded vocabulary.

direction.description: `CUSTOMER_HOLDS` - you hold underutilized value and the search finds who wants it. `CUSTOMER_SEEKS` - you would source value another company holds.

resource.description: What of YOURS the opportunity rests on.

counterpart.description: The kind of company that completes it.

markets.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 markets the counterpart search would cover.

proximity_bound.description: True when the exchange only transacts over short distances (heat, CO2, water, bulky low-value material, shared capacity), so reachability constrains the search.

grounding_sources.description: Customer-safe CATEGORIES the claims rest on - where and when, never who. Paired with the list's `computed_at`, these are the provenance of everything shown here.

outreach_draft_eligible.description: Whether this entry may GROUND an outreach draft. False when the `resource` - the thing a message would be ABOUT - is an unconfirmed hypothesis; such an entry must not be used to compose outreach in any form, not even as a question, until the customer confirms it. True does NOT license asserting the `counterpart`: that is a hypothesis about a MARKET rather than about the customer, it carries its own `speech_act`, and on a true entry it is very often still `ASK`. Read both.

requires_resource_confirmation.description: True when running this entry requires `confirmedResource` on the trigger, because its resource is an unconfirmed hypothesis.

credits_cost.description: What running the counterpart search costs, shown before anything is spent.

opportunities.description: In server-authoritative order. Never padded - an empty array means nothing is well-grounded, which is a real answer and not a failure.

computed_at.description: Epoch milliseconds when this portfolio was DERIVED. It is not recomputed to answer a read, so a value some days old is expected and is the honest date of these claims.

opted_out.description: True when you have turned circular suggestions off. The list is then empty because you asked for it to be, which is a different thing from having no opportunities.

Suggestion.description: A single customer-safe entry derived from THIS job's measured signals. Two kinds share this shape, distinguished by `code`: (1) a bounded ADVICE recommendation (never a rejection reason); and (2) a mandatory `FILTER_RELAXED` DISCLOSURE that a requested filter was relaxed to fill quota. In both cases the human-readable `message` carries the detail — no internal rejection classes, funnel counts, or structured disclosure internals are delivered. Every suggestion carries exactly `{code, message, suggested_parameters}`.

code.description: Bounded code (NOT a rejection reason). The first seven values are advice codes; `FILTER_RELAXED` is a mandatory relaxation disclosure, `TRANSIENT_INTERRUPTION` advises a plain re-run after an infra stall, `PIPELINE_LIMITED` and `ALREADY_DELIVERED` are honest non-actionable outcomes that deliberately carry NO broadening advice, and `REGION_PREFERENCE_APPLIED` is an informational note that a `sub_country_regions` preference shaped this run.

x-code-notes.TRANSIENT_INTERRUPTION: Under-delivery caused by a transient infrastructure stall (crawl-queue TTL expiry), NOT market thinness. Message-only, retry-oriented — re-running the same search will likely return more.
x-code-notes.PIPELINE_LIMITED: Under-delivery whose dominant cause was candidates WE could not turn into a usable company record — an anti-bot wall, a crawl failure, a page that was not a company, a phantom entity, or a verdict we could not reach. The customer's criteria are NOT the binding constraint, so this code deliberately carries NO `suggested_parameters` and no broadening advice: telling a customer to widen their filters to compensate for our coverage gap would be misleading.
x-code-notes.ALREADY_DELIVERED: Under-delivery whose dominant cause was candidates that MATCHED the criteria and were dropped only because they are already known — already delivered under this ICP, the customer's own domain, a competitor, or a duplicate. Supply exhaustion for this exact search profile; broadening would not have recovered them, so the code is message-only.
x-code-notes.FILTER_RELAXED: Mandatory disclosure that a requested filter (`company_sizes` or `sub_country_regions`) was relaxed so some RETURNED prospects fall outside it. The `message` states which filter and by how much; the underlying detail (violating prospects, match counts) is never delivered. Carries `suggested_parameters` clearing that filter (e.g. `{sub_country_regions: []}`) as the one-tap correction.
x-code-notes.REGION_PREFERENCE_APPLIED: Informational note emitted on a terminal run whose request carried a non-empty `sub_country_regions` when a quantified `FILTER_RELAXED` region disclosure did not fire (the region signal often finalizes only after async enrichment). Discloses that the regional filter is a PREFERENCE — in-region companies are ranked higher while out-of-region companies are still returned ranked lower — so results are more targeted but fewer. Carries the same `{sub_country_regions: []}` correction to broaden coverage across the whole country.

message.description: Customer-safe, human-readable recommendation or disclosure. Contains no internal rejection reasons or funnel counts.

suggested_parameters.description: Optional criteria changes to apply and re-run. Absent when the advice needs no parameter change.

SuggestedCriteria.description: A partial `DiscoveryCriteria` delta. Merge it over your original request (the delta wins) and start a new discovery. Every field is optional; only the changed values are present. An empty array (e.g. `sub_country_regions: []`) explicitly clears that field. When the run under-delivered, an LLM improvement pass may also rewrite the free-text `query` itself — when present, `query` REPLACES your original `query` verbatim (it is not merged token-wise); apply it alongside the other fields to re-run the improved ICP.

query.description: LLM-rewritten replacement for the free-text `query`, refined from this run's outcome to surface more matching companies. Present only when the improvement pass produced a better query; use it as-is in place of your original `query` on the re-run.

locations.description: Suggested replacement for `locations` (e.g. a wider set of countries).

sub_country_regions.description: Suggested replacement for `sub_country_regions`. An empty array clears the field.

JobState.description: Discovery lifecycle state. `queued` = accepted, not yet started; `running` and `processing` = discovery in progress; `completed` = finished and reached its target; `failed` = ended with an error; `exhausted` = finished but ran out of candidates before hitting the target; `cancelled` = stopped by the caller via `POST /mcp/jobs/{jobId}/cancel`. The last four are terminal.

ProspectList.description: A page of discovered companies (customer-safe fields only).

prospects.description: The discovered companies in this response.

total.description: PAGINATION count — the number of prospects returned in THIS list response. This is a LIST result-set count over your de-duplicated inbox (optionally scoped by `job_id`), a DIFFERENT concept from a single discovery's delivery count (`JobResult.total_prospects` / `JobStatus.total_prospects`) — do not group the two together. Named `total` to match the sibling search list (`ProspectSummaryList.total`); note that sibling counts total MATCHES (which can exceed the page), whereas this one counts the rows in this page.

customer_id.description: The authenticated tenant these prospects belong to.

suggestions.description: On the per-run view (`GET /api/v1/discoveries/{jobId}/prospects`), the same data-driven next-step recommendation(s) `JobResult.suggestions` carries — present only when the run underperformed. Empty on successful runs and on the de-duplicated `GET /api/v1/prospects` list.

ProspectDetail.description: A single company looked up by domain via `GET /api/v1/prospects/{domain}`. Returned only when the company exists for this tenant: `prospect` carries its full customer-safe record — including detail-only enrichments (such as `knowledge_graph` and `pages`) not returned by the list endpoints. An unknown domain is a `404` carrying the standard `Error` envelope (`{error: "not_found", message, request_id}`), not a `200` body.

domain.description: The domain this record was looked up by, echoed at the envelope root on every detail response — the same value as `prospect.domain`. Served so a client batching several lookups can attribute a response without reaching into the nested record.

AckRequest.description: Body for acknowledging delivery of one or more companies (batch).

domains.description:
Domains to acknowledge. Each is marked delivered so it isn't returned again across
any of your discoveries. Idempotent — acking an unknown or already-acknowledged
domain is a harmless no-op that simply contributes 0 to the count.

customer_id.description: The acknowledging customer's id (echoed from the X-Customer-Id header).

acknowledged.description:
Number of prospect records marked delivered across the requested domains. Idempotent —
unknown or already-acknowledged domains contribute 0.

matched.description:
How many of the requested domains belong to this customer (already-acknowledged ones
included). When it is 0 — every requested domain is unknown to this customer — the call
answers 404 instead of a 200 that acknowledged nothing.

requested.description: Number of domains in the request.

Contact.description:
A discovered person at the company — customer-safe fields only. Most fields are nullable
since discovery frequently yields partial data. Any field not listed here is never
returned.

email.description: The person's email address, where discovered.

position.description: The person's job title or role.

title.description: The person's job title or role, as surfaced during discovery (alternative source to `position`).

phone.description: A direct phone number for the person.

department.description: The department or function the person works in.

organization.description: The organization or company the person is associated with.

contact_address.description: The person's street address, where discovered.

contact_country_code.description: The person's country as an ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 code.

contact_region.description: The person's sub-country region (e.g. state or province).

registry_source.description: The government registry this person was verified against, when applicable.

email_source.description: Provenance of `email` when it was INFERRED rather than directly discovered. `derived_domain_pattern` = a name-coupled mailbox reconstructed from the company's own observed local-part convention (confidence ~0.5, never verified); `micro_company_generic_pairing` = a sole owner paired to the company's generic mailbox. Absent (null) for a crawled/verified email. Use it to weight an inferred address (which carries bounce risk) before outreach.

is_officer.description: True when this person matches a statutory officer listed in a government registry.

Prospect.description:
A discovered company — customer-safe fields only. Internal scoring, provenance, and raw
content fields are never present; any field not listed here is never returned. Most
fields are nullable, since discovery frequently yields partial data. `domain` is always
present. A few fields are populated only on specific endpoints, noted per-field
(e.g. `knowledge_graph`/`pages` on the detail endpoint, `semantic_score` on search).

There is deliberately no bare `source` field: a single name would be ambiguous about what
it describes. Provenance is published per subject instead: `registry_source`,
`employee_count_source`, `footer_legal_name_source` and `social_source` here, and
`email_source` on the nested `contacts` entries.

domain.description: The company's primary website domain. The stable identifier for the prospect.

description.description: Short description of what the company does.

industry.description: The company's primary industry (coarse-grained). Free-text, but normalized from a canonical taxonomy: `fashion_retail`, `electronics_retail`, `grocery_retail`, `home_furniture`, `furniture_manufacturing`, `automotive`, `manufacturing`, `chemicals_materials`, `agriculture_food_production`, `logistics`, `b2b_services`, `technology_software`, `healthcare`, `financial_services`, `cosmetics_beauty`, `jewelry_accessories`, `hospitality_restaurant`, `energy`, `sporting_goods`, `recreation`, `education`, and the specialty-retail categories `florist_flowers`, `bakery_pastry`, `butcher_delicatessen`, `optician_eyewear`, `pharmacy_drugstore`, `pet_shop`, `toy_hobby`, `stationery_office_supplies`, `bookstore`, `garden_center`, `musical_instruments`, and `hardware_diy`. The list is not strict — a value outside it may occasionally be returned — so treat it as the expected vocabulary rather than a closed enum.
