employee_count_source.description: Authority band of `employee_count` — a source-agnostic label for the kind of source that won the precedence contest when the value was last written (`official_registry` > `public_knowledge_base` > `professional_network` > `web_research` > `company_website` > `unverified_estimate`, with `verified` an operator override). `official_registry` is an official government/company registry; `public_knowledge_base` is a public, structured, source-referenced knowledge base; `professional_network` is a public professional-network profile; `web_research` is a third-party OSINT figure researched from cited public sources; `company_website` is the company's own website; `unverified_estimate` is an UNVERIFIED third-party or model-derived estimate — nothing was measured, filed or self-declared, so treat it as the pipeline's best guess and NOT as a sourced figure. Surfaced customer-side so the freshness/authority of the headcount can be audited (provenance of a delivered fact) without naming any internal pipeline/vendor. Null when no source has been recorded.

employee_count_as_of.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when `employee_count` was last written by a winning source (server-stamped). The freshness marker paired with `employee_count_source`. Null when no source has been recorded.

company_size.description: Company size bucket by employee headcount (lowercase; null when undetermined). `micro` (≤10 employees), `small` (≤50), `medium` (≤200), `large` (≤500), `enterprise` (500+). Uses the SAME lowercase tokens as the `company_sizes` INPUT filter (DiscoveryCriteria.company_sizes), so a value read off a result can be re-submitted verbatim as a filter without a 400. `micro` companies are returned by a `small` `company_sizes` filter.

headquarters_location.description: Headquarters location as a "City, Country" string.

country_code.description: The company's country as an ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 code.

state.description: The company's state, province, or region.

postal_code.description: The company's postal or ZIP code.

street_romanized.description: Latin-script transliteration of `street`, for companies in non-Latin-script markets.

company_emails.description: General company email addresses (e.g. info@, sales@), as opposed to a specific person's.

city_romanized.description: Latin-script transliteration of city (non-Latin source markets).

state_romanized.description: Latin-script transliteration of state (non-Latin source markets).

telegram_url.description: The company's Telegram channel or click-to-chat URL.

douyin_url.description: The company's Douyin (Chinese TikTok) profile URL.

wechat_id.description: WeChat account ID (WeChat has no public profile URL).

qq_id.description: QQ account ID (QQ has no public profile URL).

business_model.description: The company's classified business model — `manufacturer`, `retailer`, `distributor`, or `unknown`. Null when not classified.

estimated_annual_revenue_usd.description: Estimated annual revenue in whole USD dollars, derived from a model (based on employee count). Null when undetermined — never a fabricated zero.

estimated_revenue_currency.description: ISO-4217 alpha-3 currency for the revenue estimate (currently always USD).

founded_year.description: Year the company was founded (company-maturity signal). Null when unknown.

reported_revenue_usd.description: Reported annual revenue in whole USD dollars, sourced from public company financials (distinct from the model-based `estimated_annual_revenue_usd`). Null when not reported.

funding_total_usd.description: Total capital raised to date in whole USD dollars, from public company financials. Null when not reported.

funding_latest_round.description: Latest funding round (round name/type, date, amount, currency). Returned as a decoded object — the API decodes the stored JSON for you at the boundary, so do NOT decode a second time. The key set comes from the financial source and is not closed: read the keys you need and ignore the rest. Often null.

web_traffic.description: Website-traffic snapshot. Returned as a decoded object — the API decodes the stored JSON for you at the boundary, so do NOT decode a second time. The properties below are the ones commonly present; the key set comes from the traffic source and is not closed, so read the keys you need and ignore the rest. Often null.

visitsMonthly.description: Visits in the most recent complete month.

countryRank.description: Traffic rank of the site within its own country (lower is busier).

history.description: Month-by-month visit history, oldest period first.

hq_address.description: Full one-line formatted headquarters address (companion to city/country/postal).

source_published_date.description: Publication date of the web source this prospect was surfaced from (per-source freshness).

source_last_updated.description: Last-updated date of the web source this prospect was surfaced from (per-source freshness).

registry_id.description: The company's government registry identifier (e.g. IČO, HRB, KRS), where matched.

lei.description: Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442), where the company is present in the GLEIF register. Null otherwise.

uscc.description: Chinese Unified Social Credit Code. Populated only for Chinese companies. Null otherwise.

social_profiles.description: Per-platform public social profiles discovered for the company, beyond the singular per-platform `*_url` fields (which carry only the headline platform). One entry per platform, returned as decoded objects — the API decodes the stored JSON for you at the boundary, so do NOT decode a second time.

platform.description: Which public platform this entry is from, and the provenance for the rest of the entry's fields (e.g. `linkedin`, `youtube`, `twitter`, `instagram`).

url.description: The public profile URL on that platform.

follower_count.description: Audience size on that platform (followers, or subscribers on video platforms). Null when the profile published no count.

description.description: The company's own business summary as published on that platform, verbatim. Null when the profile published none.

legal_name.description: Registered legal-entity name CANDIDATE taken from that profile's own title or summary. A candidate only — it never overrides the company name. Null when the profile published no distinct legal name.

extra_links.description: External links the profile itself lists (subsidiary, other-market or store domains). Null for platforms that publish no such block.

employer_reputation_tier.description: Coarse, un-attributed employer-reputation band — `strong`, `mixed`, or `limited`. A derived legitimacy/size-corroboration signal; NOT a third-party review platform's verbatim rating (which is never returned) and carrying NO source name. Null when no reputation signal is available.

beian_number.description: China MIIT web-filing number (beian = the ICP备案 recordal, e.g. 湘ICP备17001547号) mined from the site footer. A MIIT-registered-commercial-site provenance signal — NOT a corporate registry id (registry_source is set to 'MIIT-BEIAN' when present).

footer_legal_name.description: Market-agnostic registered legal-name candidate anchored in the page footer / legal-notice region. Two producers today: the CN beian (ICP备案)/copyright footer (Chinese …有限公司 or English … LIMITED/LTD) and the DE/AT §5 TMG Impressum legal name (…GmbH/AG). Verbatim — never translated. A candidate that never overwrites company_name. Which producer supplied it is on footer_legal_name_source.

footer_legal_name_source.description: Where `footer_legal_name` was taken from — `beian` (Chinese MIIT web-filing footer), `impressum` (German/Austrian legal-notice footer), or `copyright` (a plain copyright line). Null when `footer_legal_name` is null.

social_description.description: Business summary harvested from the prospect's public social profile page (no login). Winning-platform priority LinkedIn > YouTube > Twitter; the source platform is on social_source.

social_follower_count.description: Audience-size traction proxy from the winning social profile — LinkedIn follower count OR YouTube subscriber count (which one is on social_source).

social_legal_name.description: Registered legal-entity name candidate from a social profile's og:title / og:description (never overwrites company_name; names never translated).

social_source.description: Which public social profile the social intel above came from — `linkedin`, `youtube`, or `twitter`. Null when no social profile was found.

social_extra_links.description: YouTube channel About-tab external links (subsidiary / other-market / store domains). A YouTube-only signal.

nace_code.description: The company's NACE industry-classification code, from its registry entry where available.

legal_form.description: The company's legal form (e.g. GmbH, s.r.o., Ltd), from its registry entry where available.

officers.description: Names of the company's statutory officers, from its government registry entry where available.

registration_date.description: Date the company was registered, from its registry entry where available.

discovered_at.description: When this company was first discovered for you (ISO-8601).

detected_language.description: ISO-639-1 language detected for the company's content.

detected_industry.description: Finer-grained detected industry (companion to the coarse `industry`). Drawn from the same canonical taxonomy listed under `industry` — including the specialty-retail categories (`florist_flowers`, `bakery_pastry`, `butcher_delicatessen`, `optician_eyewear`, `pharmacy_drugstore`, `pet_shop`, `toy_hobby`, `stationery_office_supplies`, `bookstore`, `garden_center`, `musical_instruments`, `hardware_diy`) — and likewise not a strict closed set.

company_status.description: The company's operational status, where a government registry reports it (e.g. `active`, `liquidated`, `dissolved`). Free-text — not a fixed set.

has_wikipedia_article.description: Notability / enterprise signal — a Wikipedia article was found.

domain_age_days.description: Age of the registered domain in days — company maturity/stability signal.

sub_country_region.description: The ISO-3166-2 sub-country region (e.g. `ES-VC`, `DE-BY`) the company's own headquarters geography places it in — resolved from its stored `state`, `city` and `postal_code`, so it can be checked against the address on the same record. It is the region a `sub_country_regions` discovery filter is matched against. Null when that geography does not resolve to a region; it is cleared again if a later correction to the address stops supporting it. A single HQ region, distinct from `branch_regions`.

certifications.description: Quality/compliance certifications the company publicly claims (e.g. ISO 9001:2015, IATF 16949, IPC-A-610, RoHS, REACH), extracted from the company's public web presence.

customer_count.description: Self-reported count of customers/clients served — a traction proxy (distinct from employee_count).

export_markets.description: Export / market-distribution snapshot. Returned as a decoded object — the API decodes the stored JSON for you at the boundary, so do NOT decode a second time. Two shapes are emitted depending on what the source disclosed: `{"regions":{"Europe":48,...}}` (share per region) or `{"export_share_pct":80,"regions":[...]}` (headline share plus a region list). The key set is not closed. Often null.

production_capacity.description: Manufacturing-capacity snapshot (e.g. "30,000 sq.m; 3,000 part numbers; 10+ SMT lines") — a capability signal for manufacturing/EMS prospects.

served_industries.description: Verticals/end-markets the company states it serves — a multi-value companion to detected_industry.

branch_footprint.description: Multi-site branch/office city names the company publicly lists (GeoNames-gated) — a human-readable companion to the ISO-3166-2 branch_regions.

origin_country.description: The company's inferred country of origin, as an ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 code. Helps distinguish a headquarters from a local subsidiary.

facts.description: Extracted business facts about the company — leadership, products/services, market positioning, history, and certifications — each as a short natural-language statement WITH provenance (origin + when it was extracted) for SDR briefing. Present on every prospect; an empty array when no facts are available. Capped per prospect to keep the response bounded.

text.description: The business fact, as a short natural-language statement.

source.description: Origin the fact was derived from — `web` (extracted from the company's public web content), `wikidata` (a structured Wikidata claim), or `wikipedia` (the resolved Wikipedia article).

source_url.description: Stable click-through link to the company HOMEPAGE — the entry point to the company's public web content. This is NOT necessarily the exact sub-page the fact was extracted from; the exact per-page source URL is not retained, so this field is the company homepage rather than an overclaimed extraction URL.

extracted_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when the fact was extracted.

first_party.description:
`true` when the fact is VERIFIED to come from the company's OWN web presence — a citation whose registrable (eTLD+1) domain equals the prospect's.
`false` means "not verified as first-party", which covers TWO different situations and is never a positive claim of third-party origin: the fact was mined from a third-party page (a directory, aggregator, news site or filing, and note Wikipedia/Wikidata count as third-party here however well their entity was resolved), OR its provenance cannot be established because no citation host was ever stored for it. The second case is not marginal — MEASURED on the production corpus, 46% of facts carry no stored citation host at all; they are legacy points and the inspectable sample was model-derived rather than site-derived. A consumer must therefore read `false` as "unconfirmed", not as "independently sourced".
Why it is customer-visible: a first-party claim is the company describing itself, while a third-party claim is someone else describing it, and an SDR should weigh a self-description differently from an independent one before quoting it. Third-party facts also carry the residual entity-confusion risk that first-party facts cannot: DNS ownership is collision-free, whereas a shared brand token, ticker or surname is not. Off-domain facts pass an entity-identity check, but that check can let a fact through when it is unavailable — which is exactly why the customer still gets to see the distinction.
ABSENCE IS NOT `false`. The key is omitted on facts stored before it was introduced, and such a fact's provenance is UNKNOWN, not third-party — a consumer that defaults a missing value to `false` will silently mislabel every It is therefore deliberately NOT in `required`.

knowledge_graph.description: Extracted knowledge-graph facts about the company (relationship triples). Returned only by the detail endpoint (`GET /api/v1/prospects/{domain}`).

knowledge_graph_grouped.description: The same knowledge-graph facts, grouped by relationship type for convenience. Returned only by the detail endpoint.

pages.description: References to the company web pages that were read during discovery. Returned only by the detail endpoint.

semantic_score.description: Relevance score for this company against the search query. Returned only by the search endpoint (`GET /api/v1/prospects/search`).

ProspectSummary.description:
A lean company summary returned by `GET /api/v1/prospects/search` — a deliberate subset
of `Prospect` so a search page stays small. `domain` is always present; use it with
`GET /api/v1/prospects/{domain}` to fetch the full record (contacts, emails, registry
data, social profiles, and more). Only the fields listed here are returned.

domain.description: The company's primary website domain. Use it to fetch the full record.

company_size.description: Company size bucket by employee headcount (lowercase; null when undetermined). `micro` (≤10 employees), `small` (≤50), `medium` (≤200), `large` (≤500), `enterprise` (500+). Uses the SAME lowercase tokens as the `company_sizes` INPUT filter (DiscoveryCriteria.company_sizes), so a value read off a result can be re-submitted verbatim as a filter without a 400. `micro` companies are returned by a `small` `company_sizes` filter.

headquarters_location.description: Headquarters location as a "City, Country" string.

description.description: Short teaser, capped at 200 Unicode characters (never split mid-character). When the source description exceeds the cap it is cut at a word boundary and an ellipsis (…) is appended, so a shortened teaser is always visibly marked as truncated.

semantic_score.description: Blended relevance score for this search result.

ProspectSummaryList.description: A capped page of lean search summaries with progressive-cursor pagination.

prospects.description: The lean company summaries on this page.

total.description: PAGINATION count — the number of MATCHES for this query (relevance-floor-passing results), NOT the page length. Use it for a "showing X of N" label (X = `prospects.length`, N = `total`). When `has_more` is true because deep pagination hit the recall cap, `total` is a lower bound and `has_more` signals the unreached tail. This is a SEARCH result-set count, a DIFFERENT concept from a single discovery's delivery count (`JobResult.total_prospects` / `JobStatus.total_prospects`) — do not group the two together. (Contrast `ProspectList.total`, which is the same NAME but counts the rows in the returned page rather than all matches.)

query.description: Echo of the `q` that produced this page.

has_more.description: True when another page exists above the relevance floor. False means you have seen everything relevant — stop paging.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page (pass back as `cursor`); null at the terminus.

truncated.description: True when a hard item/byte cap dropped rows from THIS page (distinct from `has_more`, which signals whether more pages remain).
